catalogue.note: Built at Figma’s own 390 wide and own height: every size in the frame is a whole number, no scale to recover. Square and unframed: Figma’s 1px black outside stroke on the frame is left off, so the diff runs on the 390-wide region inside it (the export is 2px larger each way). Inter Regular and Bold, as Figma names them, from the Inter Variable 4.001 file on this Mac, embedded whole; the width probe shows Inter rendering. Every text box matches Figma’s position and size; flat colours are exact; what differs is glyph-edge antialiasing. The circled i is not in Inter: it is the outline from Figma’s SVG export of that text, in the same place. “0×8f4a”: the layer says 0x8f4a and Figma’s older Inter turns the x between digits into a multiplication sign; Inter 4 does not, so the sign is written out. Dashed rules are drawn as Figma draws them: one row above their slot, pattern fitted to the length.
